releaseNotes: machine/ is complete — the eval harness moves in with the validators it serves. 129 eval files (evals/launchbench 115, evals/agent-behavior 13, evals/triggering 1) become machine/evals/, scripts/fixtures/ becomes machine/fixtures/, and the four eval runners (run-launchbench, run-agent-evals, run-behavioral-evals, run-validator-fixtures) move to machine/. This closes ARCHITECTURE.md's migration order: every top-level directory now answers who reads it rather than what kind of file it holds.

run-audit.ts deliberately stays in scripts/. It is the pipeline orchestrator that runs everything — gates, machine checks and renderers alike — not part of the eval harness, and ARCHITECTURE.md's machine/ enumeration (versioning, evals, parity, fixtures) does not name it. The residue left in scripts/ is now coherent: everything executable that is neither a gate nor the eval harness.

The trap fixed in v0.55.0 recurred one directory move later, exactly as predicted. check-package-parity located run-launchbench.ts with a hardcoded path.join(skillRoot, "scripts", "run-launchbench.ts"); once that runner moved to machine/, existsSync went false and checkLaunchbenchValidatorParity returned early — silently skipping the entire knownValidators cross-check while still exiting 0. Same silent-no-op shape as the regex bug, but at the file-locate step rather than inside the loop, and inside the very function whose comment describes fixing that class of bug for its internal lookups only. It now resolves through findScriptPath.

check-reference-size gained a directory-level exemption rather than 129 files gaining an index. Its KNOWLEDGE_ROOTS already included machine/, and collectFilesRecursive collects .md AND .yaml, so moving the evals in would have subjected them to the per-file byte budget and — the real blocker — to checkDirectoryIndex, which demands every directory holding .md/.yaml carry an index linking each child. machine/evals/launchbench/ would have needed a README linking all 115 scenarios. EXCLUSIONS is keyed on basename and cannot express that. NON_KNOWLEDGE_DIRS exempts machine/evals/ and machine/fixtures/ on the same stated rationale source-registry.yaml already carries: machine-read data consumed by a harness that globs the directory, never loaded into agent context as prose. This preserves behaviour rather than relaxing it — both trees sat outside every knowledge root before the move, and widening these gates to cover fixtures would be its own change with its own evidence.

audit-skill-links needed no change, which was verified rather than assumed. Its orphan gate scans machine/ with collectAllFiles and no extension filter, so all 129 eval files newly entered its scope; it passes because isReachable accepts a mention of a file's parent directory and the runners name the eval directories. Only the gate that actually broke was touched.

Two path forms were invisible to a slash-shaped search and are recorded because this pattern keeps recurring: run-behavioral-evals.ts and check-workflow-adherence.ts both build eval paths with path.join(skillRoot, "evals", "launchbench") style bare segments. The behavioral-results output path is the more dangerous of the two — it has no existsSync guard, so left unfixed it would have written results into a stale orphaned directory instead of failing. Conversely "launchbench" in audit-plan.ts and check-package-parity.ts is an npm SCRIPT NAME and "fixtures" in script-paths.ts is a NOT_SPAWNABLE set member; both look like path segments and must never be rewritten.
